s:
Under the erstwhile Plan and non-Plan classification of government expenditure, Plan expenditure comprised:
1. Expenditure on Central Plans
2. Central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans
3. Interest payments on public debt
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Plan expenditure covered Central Plans and central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans. Interest payments were classified as non-Plan expenditure.
tq: Separate the two components of the former Plan category from a familiar non-Plan item.
sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following was a non-Plan expenditure item under the former classification?
o: Expenditure on a new Central Plan
Central assistance for Union Territory Plans
x: Interest payments formed part of the larger non-Plan expenditure category. Central Plans and central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans were Plan expenditure.
tq: Use the direct association between interest payments and the former non-Plan category.
sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following sets contains only items classified as non-Plan expenditure under the former system?
o: Interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries and pensions
Central Plans, defence, subsidies, salaries and pensions
Central assistance for State Plans, pensions, salaries and interest payments
Central Plans, Central assistance for Union Territory Plans and defence
x: Interest payments, defence, subsidies, salaries, pensions and maintenance of assets created in earlier Plans were non-Plan items. Central Plans and central assistance for State or Union Territory Plans were Plan items.
tq: Check every item in a set against the former classification rather than identifying only one familiar item.
sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

s: The classification of expenditure into Plan and non-Plan was discontinued from which Budget year?
x: The Plan and non-Plan classification ended from Budget 2017-18 on the recommendation of the Expenditure Management Commission.
tq: Distinguish the discontinuation year from adjacent Budget years.
sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

s: The Plan and non-Plan classification was replaced primarily by which classification?
x: After the discontinuation of Plan and non-Plan expenditure, the revenue-capital classification became the principal framework.
tq: Discriminate between two different expenditure classifications that are commonly interchanged.
sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following statements about the Union Budget changes associated with the end of Plan and non-Plan classification is correct?
o: The Railway Budget was abolished and the Budget was presented on 15 August.
The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 31 March.
The Railway Budget was separated and the Budget was presented on 1 April.
The Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget and the Budget was presented on 1 February.
x: The relevant Budget changes included the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget and presentation of the Union Budget on 1 February.
tq: Pair the two associated procedural changes instead of selecting only one of them.
sec: Plan vs non-plan expenditure - items and end of the classification  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding developmental and non-developmental expenditure:
List-I (Category)
 a. Developmental expenditure
 b. Non-developmental expenditure
 c. Economic and social services
 d. Routine operational spending
List-II (Description)
 i. Defence, interest payments and pensions
 ii. Education, health, irrigation and agriculture
 iii. A component of developmental expenditure
 iv. Consumptive expenditure required for routine operations
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Developmental expenditure includes education, health, irrigation and agriculture; non-developmental expenditure includes defence, interest payments and pensions. Economic and social services are developmental, while routine operational spending is consumptive.
tq: Start with the sure pair linking education and health to developmental expenditure.
sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT generally classified as developmental expenditure?
x: Defence is classified as non-developmental expenditure. Rural development, social welfare and public health are developmental activities.
tq: Find the item outside the growth and quality-of-life group.
sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding developmental expenditure:
1. It includes expenditure on education and health.
2. It includes expenditure on employment and rural development.
3. It is intended to stimulate growth, employment and quality of life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly describe developmental expenditure and its principal objectives.
tq: Recognise that the functional list and the stated economic purpose belong to the same category.
sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following combinations consists entirely of non-developmental expenditure items?
o: Interest payments, police and law and order, tax-collection charges
Employment, rural development and public health
x: Interest payments, police and law and order, tax-collection charges and administrative expenditure are non-developmental items.
tq: Classify the entire combination, not merely the first item.
sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): Developmental expenditure is associated with improvement in employment and quality of life.
Reason (R): It includes economic and social services such as education, health, irrigation and rural development.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true, and the inclusion of economic and social services explains why developmental expenditure improves employment and quality of life.
tq: Test whether the functional examples in the Reason explain the stated outcome in the Assertion.
sec: Developmental vs non-developmental expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the revenue-capital classification?
o: Maintenance of existing assets — Capital expenditure
Loans and advances to States — Capital expenditure
x: Loans and advances to States are capital expenditure because they affect the Government's financial assets. Maintenance of existing assets and interest payments are revenue expenditure, while repayment of loans reduces liabilities and is capital expenditure.
tq: Use the effect on assets or liabilities to identify the correct classification.
sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s: A government expenditure creates a new asset or reduces an existing liability. Under the revenue-capital distinction, it is ordinarily treated as:
x: Capital expenditure either creates assets or reduces liabilities. Revenue expenditure generally neither creates an asset nor reduces a liability.
tq: Apply the asset-liability test instead of relying on the department incurring the expenditure.
sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Grants to State governments remain revenue expenditure even if the States use them to create assets.
2. Purchase of defence equipment can be capital outlay.
3. Subsidies are ordinarily classified as capital expenditure because they support production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Grants to State governments are revenue expenditure even when they create assets for the States, and defence equipment can be capital outlay. Subsidies are revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure.
tq: Identify the exception concerning grants and reject the reversed treatment of subsidies.
sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is correctly classified as revenue expenditure?
o: Loan advanced to a public sector undertaking
x: Maintenance of existing assets is revenue expenditure. Construction of an airport, repayment of loans and loans to public sector undertakings are capital expenditure.
tq: Distinguish ordinary maintenance from expenditure that creates assets or reduces liabilities.
sec: Revenue vs capital expenditure - classifying items  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is an example of an implicit or hidden subsidy?
o: A fertiliser subsidy shown in the Budget
An export incentive shown as a Budget provision
A food subsidy shown as a separate Budget line item
Under-pricing of higher education in a public university
x: Under-pricing of publicly provided services, such as higher education in public universities, is an implicit or hidden subsidy. Food, fertiliser and export incentives shown in the Budget are explicit subsidies.
tq: Distinguish a visible Budget line item from under-pricing of a publicly provided service.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following sets contains only explicit subsidies?
o: Food, fertiliser, LPG and interest subvention
Public university education, irrigation water and public health
Irrigation water, LPG and higher education
x: Food, fertiliser, LPG, export incentives and interest subvention are explicit subsidies because they are shown as Budget line items. The other listed services are examples of hidden subsidies when under-priced.
tq: Use the visibility-in-the-Budget test to separate explicit from hidden subsidies.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: Under the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme, subsidy is fixed with reference to:
o: The quantity of food grains procured by the Government
The quantity of specified nutrients in decontrolled P&K fertilisers
The retail price of urea alone
The international price of crude oil
x: NBS fixes subsidy per kilogram of nutrient in decontrolled phosphorus- and potassium-based fertilisers. Urea is outside the NBS framework.
tq: Link the scheme name to its nutrient-based calculation rather than to the price of a single fertiliser.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: The Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme was introduced from:
x: The Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme commenced on 1 April 2010.
tq: Discriminate the notified commencement date from adjacent years.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme is correct?
o: It covers only urea and excludes all P&K fertilisers.
It covers 22 grades, including DAP, MOP and SSP, while urea remains outside it.
It applies only to one grade of fertiliser and fixes subsidy per tonne of crude oil.
It covers all fertilisers, including urea, without reference to nutrient content.
x: NBS covers 22 grades of decontrolled P&K fertilisers, including DAP, MOP and SSP, and fixes subsidy per kilogram of N, P, K and S nutrients. Urea is outside the scheme.
tq: Separate the covered P&K grades and nutrients from the excluded fertiliser, urea.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: The Oil Pool Account associated with the Administered Price Mechanism was dismantled in:
x: The Oil Pool Account under the Administered Price Mechanism was dismantled in April 2002.
tq: Use the precise month-year combination to avoid confusing the reform with neighbouring years.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: After the dismantling of the Oil Pool Account, later under-recoveries of oil companies were compensated through:
x: Later petroleum under-recoveries were compensated through oil bonds.
tq: Match the petroleum under-recovery mechanism with its specific compensation instrument.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following principles was associated with the approach of the Sixteenth Finance Commission towards subsidies?
1. Retaining only well-targeted subsidies
2. Providing exclusion criteria and sunset clauses
3. Permitting off-budget financing of subsidies without restriction
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The approach supports well-targeted subsidies, exclusion criteria and sunset clauses. It does not support unrestricted off-budget financing of subsidies.
tq: Identify the negative statement that reverses the Commission's transparency and targeting principles.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: In Budget 2026-27, the total subsidy provision was approximately:
x: The total subsidy provision in Budget 2026-27 was ₹4,54,773 crore, representing a 3.1 per cent decline from the 2025-26 revised estimate.
tq: Read the exact Budget figure and distinguish it from closely spaced alternatives.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: In Budget 2026-27, food and fertiliser subsidies together accounted for approximately what share of the total subsidy bill?
x: Food subsidy of ₹2,27,629 crore and fertiliser subsidy of ₹1,70,799 crore together accounted for 87 per cent of the total subsidy bill.
tq: Combine the two stated major heads and compare their aggregate share with the total bill.
sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: The major subsidies comprising food, fertiliser and petroleum in Budget 2026-27 were estimated at approximately what share of GDP?
x: Food, fertiliser and petroleum subsidies together amounted to about ₹4.11 lakh crore, equivalent to 1.0 per cent of GDP.

sec: Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account  [APPSC]

s: The Centre plus States public expenditure to GDP ratio was approximately what in the Economic Survey 2016-17?
x: Public expenditure of the Centre and States together was about 28 per cent of GDP in the Economic Survey 2016-17.
tq: Identify the combined-government ratio rather than a Union-only expenditure ratio.

s: According to Union Budget Estimates 2026-27, total expenditure was approximately:
x: The Union Budget Estimates 2026-27 placed total expenditure at ₹53,47,315 crore, or 13.6 per cent of GDP.
tq: Use the exact total expenditure figure and avoid confusing it with the revenue or capital components.
sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly represents the Union Budget Estimates 2026-27?
o: Revenue expenditure 3.1% of GDP and capital expenditure 10.5% of GDP
Revenue expenditure 7.7% of GDP and capital expenditure 13.6% of GDP
Revenue expenditure 13.6% of GDP and capital expenditure 10.5% of GDP
Revenue expenditure 10.5% of GDP and capital expenditure 3.1% of GDP
x: Revenue expenditure was estimated at ₹41.25 lakh crore, or 10.5 per cent of GDP, while capital expenditure was ₹12.22 lakh crore, or 3.1 per cent of GDP.
tq: Keep the revenue and capital ratios paired with their correct expenditure heads.
sec: Public expenditure trends - expenditure-GDP ratio, largest items, committed expenditure  [APPSC]

s: In the 2026-27 Union Budget expenditure composition, the largest share was assigned to:
x: States' share of taxes accounted for 22 per cent of the expenditure composition, followed by interest at 20 per cent and central sector schemes at 17 per cent.

A. Defence
B. Central Sector Schemes
C. Interest

x: The shares were States' share of taxes 22 per cent, interest 20 per cent, Central Sector Schemes 17 per cent and defence 11 per cent.

x: Interest payments of ₹14,03,972 crore represented 26 per cent of total expenditure and 40 per cent of revenue receipts.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the trend in interest payments as a share of revenue receipts?

s: Which statement correctly represents the trend in Union revenue expenditure as a percentage of GDP?

It declined from 13.6% in FY22 to 10.9% in FY25.
It remained unchanged at 13.6% between FY22 and FY25.
It increased from 10.9% in FY22 to 13.6% in FY25.

s:
Which of the following statements regarding State government expenditure is correct?
1. States' spending was between 16.15 per cent and 17.49 per cent of GSDP during 2014-24.
2. Revenue expenditure constituted 80-87 per cent of total expenditure.
3. Committed expenditure plus subsidies constituted 51.76 per cent of revenue expenditure in FY24.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements correctly describe the stated expenditure pattern of States: spending of 16.15-17.49 per cent of GSDP, revenue expenditure of 80-87 per cent of total expenditure, and 51.76 per cent for committed expenditure plus subsidies in FY24.
tq: Verify each numerical range and the specific FY24 percentage before choosing the combined code.

s: State government total expenditure as a percentage of GDP changed from FY19 to FY24 in which manner?
x: Total expenditure of States declined from 15.7 per cent of GDP in FY19 to 15.4 per cent in FY24.
tq: Compare the two specified years and retain the correct direction of movement.

s: Which of the following correctly defines effective capital expenditure?
o: Capital expenditure plus grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets
Revenue expenditure plus loans to State Governments
Capital expenditure minus grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets
Capital outlay plus interest payments on public debt
x: Effective capital expenditure is calculated as capital expenditure plus grants-in-aid for the creation of capital assets.
tq: Test the exact formula by distinguishing additions from deductions.

s: The effective capital expenditure provided for in BE 2026-27 is approximately:

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets account for ₹4.93 lakh crore of effective capital expenditure in BE 2026-27.
2. Effective capital expenditure is estimated to be 101.1 per cent of the fiscal deficit.
3. Effective capital expenditure excludes grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because effective capital expenditure includes such grants-in-aid.
tq: Find the statement that reverses the stated definition and test the two linked numerical facts.

s:
With reference to capital expenditure in the Union Budget, consider the following statements:
1. Capital expenditure is ₹12,21,821 crore.
2. Capital outlay forms the larger component of this capital expenditure.
3. Loans account for ₹2,78,780 crore of the capital expenditure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Capital expenditure of ₹12,21,821 crore comprises capital outlay of ₹9,43,042 crore and loans of ₹2,78,780 crore.
tq: Split the aggregate into its two components before selecting the coded option.

23.7 per cent in April-November 2025 and 28 per cent in Q1 2026-27

tq: Match each growth rate with its correct time period instead of comparing the figures alone.

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Body)
a. Expenditure Reforms Commission
b. Expenditure Management Commission

List-II (Year and Chairperson)
i. 2000 - K.P. Geethakrishnan
ii. 2014 - Bimal Jalan
iii. 2000 - Bimal Jalan
iv. 2014 - K.P. Geethakrishnan
x: The Expenditure Reforms Commission was constituted in February 2000 under K.P. Geethakrishnan, while the Expenditure Management Commission was associated with 2014 and chaired by Bimal Jalan.
tq: Start from the sure chairperson-year pair and eliminate the swapped combinations.
sec: Expenditure reform bodies - chairpersons

s: The Expenditure Reforms Commission, constituted in February 2000, was chaired by:
x: The chairperson was K.P. Geethakrishnan. The initials are sometimes incorrectly written as K.R.; the correct initials are K.P.
tq: Discriminate between closely similar initials in a proper name.
sec: Expenditure reform bodies - chairpersons

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Bimal Jalan in the context of expenditure-related reform bodies?
o: He chaired the Expenditure Reforms Commission in February 2000.
He chaired the Peacock-Wiseman Committee in the United Kingdom in 1961.
He chaired the Expenditure Management Commission associated with 2014.
He formulated Wagner’s law in the nineteenth century.
x: Bimal Jalan chaired the Expenditure Management Commission associated with 2014. He should not be confused with K.P. Geethakrishnan, who chaired the Expenditure Reforms Commission.
tq: Use the wrong-person-for-the-deed trap to separate two chairpersons.
sec: Expenditure reform bodies - chairpersons

s: Wagner’s law states that, as an economy industrialises:
o: Public expenditure rises faster than national income
Public expenditure falls faster than national income
Public expenditure rises only during wars and crises
Public expenditure remains constant irrespective of national income
x: Wagner’s law, also called the law of increasing state activity, holds that public expenditure rises faster than national income as an economy industrialises.
tq: Match the law with its distinctive continuous income-related trend.
sec: Wagner's law and Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis

s: Which of the following best describes the Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis?
o: Public expenditure rises in steps, particularly during wars and crises, and generally does not return to its earlier level.
Public expenditure declines whenever the tolerable tax burden increases.
Public expenditure rises continuously and smoothly with national income.
Public expenditure is unrelated to taxation and national emergencies.
x: The Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis, based on UK data and associated with 1961, states that public spending rises in steps during wars and crises and does not fully fall back afterwards.
tq: Identify the stepwise pattern and the lasting effect rather than Wagner’s continuous-rise formulation.
sec: Wagner's law and Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis

s: The displacement effect in public expenditure theory is associated with:
o: The fiscal multiplier of capital expenditure
x: The displacement effect is associated with the Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis. Wars and crises raise the tolerable tax burden and displace public spending to a higher level.
tq: Discriminate between the two theories using their signature concepts.
sec: Wagner's law and Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Wagner’s law from the Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis?
o: Wagner’s law concerns continuous growth of public expenditure with industrialisation, whereas Peacock-Wiseman concerns stepwise increases caused by wars and crises.
Wagner’s law concerns stepwise spending after crises, whereas Peacock-Wiseman concerns continuous growth with income.
Both theories state that public expenditure falls after a crisis.
Both theories are concerned exclusively with subsidy expenditure.
x: Wagner’s law links the continuous rise of public expenditure with industrialisation and income, whereas Peacock-Wiseman explains discontinuous increases through crises and the displacement effect.
tq: Place the two similar theories side by side and identify their defining contrast.
sec: Wagner's law and Peacock-Wiseman hypothesis

s: The Golden Rule in the context of public finance emphasises that government borrowing should ordinarily be used for:
o: Payment of all routine salaries and pensions
Creation of assets through capital expenditure
Financing every form of revenue expenditure
x: The Golden Rule emphasises borrowing only for asset creation, making the quality and composition of spending more important than its size alone.
tq: Apply the rule to distinguish asset-creating expenditure from routine revenue expenditure.
sec: Universal angles

o: A crude-oil-driven subsidy overshoot of about ₹50,000 crore
A complete elimination of petroleum-related subsidies
A fertilizer-subsidy reduction of exactly ₹50,000 crore
A crude-oil-driven subsidy undershoot of about ₹50,000 crore

tq: Watch the direction of change and the approximate amount in a current-affairs figure.

x: Nine of the 18 large States budgeted revenue deficits for 2026-27.
tq: Convert the fraction-like current-affairs statement into an exact count.
sec: Universal angles

s: In Andhra Pradesh, the capital outlay provided in BE 2026-27 was:

s: Which of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s committed expenditure is correct?
o: Committed spending accounts for 75.3 per cent of revenue receipts and consists exclusively of capital outlay.
Committed spending accounts for 55.3 per cent of revenue receipts and eliminates revenue expenditure.
Committed spending accounts for 45.3 per cent of revenue receipts and leaves ample room for capex.
Committed spending accounts for 65.3 per cent of revenue receipts and leaves little room for additional spending flexibility.
